label: v136
changes: A family status — one line at the top of the home screen for whatever's happening right now. "Everyone at Oma's until Sunday." "Mia has chickenpox, don't visit." It shows who wrote it and when. It replaces rather than piles up, so it stays something you read at a glance instead of another feed to keep up with. Business spaces get it too.
Fixed: tapping the family photo opened the menu instead of the photo. That was my mistake when the header was rebuilt. It opens the photo again.
The family photo in the header is bigger.

The sections menu is grouped now — Everyday, Documents & IDs, Money & cover, Home & things, Memories — with Family and Emergency pinned at the top. Twenty-one sections in one flat list meant you had to already know the app to find anything.
On a phone it opens as a full sheet instead of a small panel with a hidden cap, so you can see there's more below rather than having to guess.
And there's a search box at the top of it: type three letters instead of reading the whole list.

Fixed: our privacy note claimed that opening your files always requires signing in. That wasn't true — an uploaded document has a private link that works on its own, which is what makes sharing and exporting work. The note now says so plainly, so you can judge for yourself how to treat a backup.
Backup files no longer carry those direct links to your documents. The documents themselves are still in the backup; the links were an extra copy of the key, travelling with the lock.
Removed personal email addresses that were being shipped inside the app's code.

"Needs attention" now ranks by how soon something actually needs you, not just by how loud it is. A passport expiring on Friday could previously fall out of the visible six while a long-dead one sat above it.
A birthday is no longer announced three times on one screen. The gift reminder now stops on the day itself, where it had nothing left to suggest.
The "add to Home Screen" card now sits at the bottom of the screen instead of appearing at the top two seconds after you started reading and pushing everything down.
